full_judgment:
6. Mr Tufailur Rahman the learned Advocate appearing with Ms Afreen Mohiuddin on behalf of the appellants submits that the impugned judgment and decree is not sustainable in law in that the suit itself was barred under Article 86 of the Limitation Act. The learned Advocate appearing for the appellants submits that the claim of the plaintiff is not sustainable both in law as well as in facts in as much as the fire alleged to have taken place in the premises of the godown which was not covered by the Insurance Policy granted by the defendant Nos.1-3. 

 8. Mr Fazlul Haque the learned Advocate appearing with Mr Akbar Hossain, on the other hand, submits that the incident of fire took place in the suit premises on 21-2-97 at 12-30 hours out of electric short-circuit and the fire broke out at the godown premise of M/s Golden Twisting Factory namely the plaintiff and immediately thereafter Munshiganj Fire Station was informed about the incident on the same day which having arrived at the scene tried their best to extinguish the fire and before the said fire came under control the entire stocks in the godown were completely gutted; a GD entry with Munshiganj Police Station was, also lodged in connection with the same incident on 22-2-97 bearing No.741 and that the mortgagee bank of the insured property namely Agrani Bank Mukterpur Branch notified the defendant Nos.1-3 about the incident by their letter No.95-97 dated 22-2-97 and the plaintiff lodged a formal claim with the Sadharan Bima Corporation for loss on 3-3-97 whereupon the defendant Nos.1-3 appointed surveyors Ms. Asian Survey and M/s Udoyan Survey for inspection. The said surveyors having conducted survey about the loss as claimed by the plaintiff submit- ted their report recommending the claim of the plaintiff to the defendant Nos. 1-3, moreover there were other reports from different other agencies supporting the claim of the plaintiff, despite such a position the defendants kept silence and ultimately on 9-3-2000 refused the claim of the plaintiff, therefore, the cause of action of the suit arose on 9-3-2000 and thereafter the instant suit was instituted on 7-8-2000, therefore, the learned Advocate for the respondents submits that the question of limitation as contemplated under clause (b) of Article 86 of the Limitation Act does not arise at all. 

 13. The pertinent question raised about the applicability of clause (b) of Article 86 of the Limitation Act which prescribes a period of 3(three) years from the date of the occurrence causing the loss. Before entering into further discussion of the same we feel it proper to quote the relevant law which reads as under:- 

 Period of Limitation 

 15. In appreciating such submission made by the learned Advocate we find that the entire gamut can be unfolded if the law as quoted above, is read together with first part of clause (b) of Article 86 of the Limitation Act which shows that the question of proof of the quantum of loss is very much pertinent and in determining the quantum of loss the question of assessment and evaluation and verification about the claim ought to have been made as it has been done in the instant case by two surveyors as also by the police officer during investigation including the Fire Service men and up on accumulating all those report the quantum of loss can be assessed which necessarily take sufficient time for the purpose, therefore, before assessment of a claim for specific amount cannot be made by the plaintiff and that too has to be either accepted or refused by the insurer himself, in the event of acceptance of the claim no question of filing of a suit arises rather it is only in the event of refusal of claim, institution of suit necessitates. 

 16. In the instant case we find that the cause of action of the suit necessarily arose on the date of refusal of the claim of the plaintiff by defendant Nos.1-3 on 9-3-2000 and the suit was instituted on 7-8-2000 and that before refusal of the claim of the plaintiff by the defendant a cause of action does not arise and a suit cannot be instituted, therefore, in our opinion, the law of limitation as quoted above, runs from the cause of action of a suit and that should be in all cases for 3 (three) years not from the date of occurrence as submitted by the learned Advocate for the appellants, therefore, we find that the instant suit has been filed well within the prescribed period of limitation as such in no way hit by clause (b) of Article 86 the limitation Act. Since all the questions raised by the learned Advocate for the appellants have already been answered therefore, in our opinion, the appeal itself is without substance.
